# Design notes (v0.1, early beta)

## Records (all generated by `src/plugin/EmberSmithing.Generator`)

| EditorID pattern | Type | Count | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EMB_HeatTempered<Weapon>`, `EMB_EmberForged<Weapon>`, `EMB_Dragonfire<Weapon>` | WEAP | 126 | Heat-tempered copies of 42 vanilla weapons. |
| `EMB_Ember/Hearth/BellowsEngraved<Armor>` | ARMO | 51 | Engraved copies of 17 vanilla armor pieces. They point at the vanilla piece as their template, like vanilla enchanted armor does, and reuse its armor addons and meshes. |
| `EMB_Ember/Hearth/BellowsEngraving` + `...EngravingEffect` | ENCH + MGEF | 3 + 3 | Constant-effect enchantments on the engraved armor (new value-modifier effects, so no vanilla effect is reused or changed). |
| `EMB_Recipe*` | COBJ (forge) | 177 | Tier and engraving recipes, keyword `CraftingSmithingForge`. |
| `EMB_Temper*` | COBJ (grindstone / workbench) | 177 | Tempering recipes for every new item, keywords `CraftingSmithingSharpeningWheel` and `CraftingSmithingArmorTable`. |

537 records, FormIDs 0x800–0xA18. The ESL range allows 0x800–0xFFF (2048 records), so the plugin stays ESL-flagged with plenty of room.

## Recipe conditions

- Forge recipes: `GetItemCount <starting item> >= 1` (only listed while you carry it), `GetBaseActorValue Smithing >= 20 / 45 / 70` (tiers) or `>= 30` (engravings), and `HasPerk <material perk>` (none for iron, hide and leather).
- Tempering recipes: the vanilla rule, `EPTemperingItemIsEnchanted == 0 OR HasPerk ArcaneBlacksmith`. The new items keep the vanilla material keywords, so the vanilla smithing perks double tempering on them as usual.

## Where the item data comes from

The new weapons and armor have to repeat the vanilla item's data (mesh, sounds, impact data, keywords, armor addons, animation type and so on), because each new record has to carry its full item data. `src/plugin/vanilla-items.json` holds that data:

- **Stats** (damage, weight, value, speed, reach, stagger, armor rating) are the vanilla values from UESP's tables.
- **Structural fields** (FormID references and mesh paths) were read from a text export of the vanilla records. Every one of the 184 referenced vanilla FormIDs was checked against Mutagen's Skyrim SE FormKey list for the right record type.
- Two `Update.esm` keywords on vanilla steel, orcish and hide armor were dropped, because the plugin's only master is Skyrim.esm. What they're used for wasn't verified, so anything that looks for them won't see them on the engraved copies.
- Critical damage is half the base damage (rounded down), as for vanilla weapons.

## Scaled down from the concept (documented on purpose)

- **Coverage**: 42 weapons and 17 armor pieces, not every vanilla item. Daggers, bows, Daedric weapons, helmets, gauntlets and boots are left for later versions; each needs per-item data that has to be checked by hand.
- **Engravings on armor only**: weapon enchantments need charge and soul-gem handling to feel right, so weapons get heat-tempering and armor gets engravings.
- **No new meshes or textures**: the tiers and engravings look exactly like the vanilla item. The name tells them apart.
